inputs by those paths; do not guess paths from names. Where the task names an

Your working directory is the repository checkout for this step. If your role
cannot write, the checkout is read-only and you must not try to change it. If it
can, commit your work to the current branch with clear messages. Never push,
open pull requests or merge: the engine does that. Write the files the task asks
you to produce into your output folder, whose path the engine gives you with the
inputs manifest.

- `outcome`: exactly one of the outcomes your task declares.
- `summary`: a short plain-text account of what you did or what stopped you, at
  most 2 KB. Later steps and people read it. If the outcome sends work back to
  another step, write the summary for that step: say what is wrong and what
  would make it right.
- `outputs`: the values your task asks you to publish, with exactly the types it
  gives.
- `artifacts`: the paths, relative to your output folder, of the files your task

any implementation. Requirements state observable behaviour the ticket must
deliver. Acceptance criteria state the conditions that satisfy them and how each
will be verified. You change no code.

|---|---|

   Each requirement supports a requirement above it (from the parent's plan, when

   this ticket as owner, copy each one with its `id` and `supports` unchanged and
   no `owner`; you may sharpen its wording, not its meaning. Keep every link a
   copied criterion has; you may add links from it to your own requirements.

   verification method: `kind: parsed_test`, this repository, a tier from step 2,

   methods later.

| Outcome | When | Artifacts |
|---|---|---|

# Add DELETE /widgets/{id}

Add an endpoint that deletes a widget by its id.

## Acceptance criteria
- `DELETE /widgets/{id}` removes the widget and returns 204 No Content when a widget with that id exists; a later `GET /widgets/{id}` returns 404.
- `DELETE /widgets/{id}` returns 404 when no widget has that id.
- `WidgetStore` gains a thread-safe way to remove a widget by id.
- Unit tests (category `unit`) cover both cases.

# The repository manifest (Feature Flow docs/07 section 4), read by the engine at each step.
api_version: feature-flow/v1
kind: repository

# No `environment` section: the sandbox uses the installation's image, which has no .NET SDK,
# so both tiers run in CI and there are no setup commands. A repository image must be built on
# the sandbox image's contract and allowed by the installation (Feature Flow docs/07 section 4,
# LOG 440 to 442).

test_tiers:
  - name: unit
    tags: [unit]
    command: dotnet test tests/FeatureFlow.Example.Api.UnitTests --filter Category=unit --logger trx --results-directory artifacts
    result: { format: trx, path: "artifacts/*.trx" }
    targets: [ci]
    ci: { job: unit.yml }

  - name: integration
    tags: [integration]
    command: docker compose -f compose.integration.yaml up --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from integration-tests
    targets: [ci]
    ci: { job: integration.yml }

static_analysis:
  analyser: none

---
name: verification
description: How requirements, acceptance criteria, verification methods, evidence claims and test results connect, with the exact document formats. Read before writing or checking any of them.
---

# Verification

## The chain

```text
requirement        requirements       observable behaviour; links up with supports
  └─ criterion     delivery_plan      an observable condition; supports requirements
      └─ method    delivery_plan      the repository and test tier that will prove it
          └─ claim evidence_claims    the exact tests the implementer says prove it
              └─ result  test_results the engine's own observation: passed or not
```

The engine checks structure, links, ownership and whether claimed tests passed.
Whether the requirements are the right ones, and whether a test's assertions
really show the behaviour, is judgement: a reviewer's or a person's.

## requirements

```yaml
schema: 1
scope: { kind: ticket, id: CLAIMS-1 }     # project | epic | ticket
requirements:
  - id: VR-001
    title: Reject expired claims
    behaviour: Submitting a claim after its deadline returns claim_expired.
    supports:
      - { artifact: requirements, requirement: VR-EPIC-03 }   # artifact: a consumed artifact's name
```

- A requirement states behaviour. It names no test, tier or design.
- It `supports` requirements above it, or gives a `supports_reason` (enabling
  work). Not both.
- Only a project-scope document names an `owner` per item: an epic, or the
  project itself, as `owner: { kind: epic, id: <the epic's name in the work list> }`
  or `owner: { kind: project, id: <the project's id> }`.

## delivery_plan

```yaml
schema: 1
scope: { kind: ticket, id: CLAIMS-1 }
acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC-001
    title: Expired claims are rejected
    behaviour: The API returns claim_expired and the stored total is unchanged.
    supports:
      - { artifact: requirements, requirement: VR-001 }
    verification:
      - id: component
        kind: parsed_test
        repository: claims-api
        tier: component
        intent: Exercise the endpoint against the real database.
        allowed_test_changes: [new, reused]
        semantic_review: required
```

- Every method is required. A method is named `<criterion>/<method>`.
- `tier` is a tier name or tag from the repository manifest. Check the baseline
  results: a tier that runs but produces no parsed results cannot prove anything.
- Only an epic-scope document names an `owner` per criterion (a ticket, or the
  epic), as `owner: { kind: ticket, id: <the ticket's name in the work list> }`.
  An owned criterion has no methods: its owner adds them.

## Ownership across levels

A parent's planner gives each item exactly one owner. A child copies every item
it owns, with `id` and `supports` unchanged and no `owner`, and holds none that
another owns. An epic copies requirements word for word; a ticket may sharpen a
criterion's wording but not its meaning. A child that owns nothing cannot run.

## evidence_claims

```yaml
schema: 1
claims:
  - criterion: AC-001
    verification: component
    tests:
      - repository: claims-api
        tier: component
        id: Claims.ExpiredClaimIsRejected          # exactly as in the parsed results
        source: { file: tests/ClaimsTests.cs, symbol: ExpiredClaimIsRejected }
        change: new                                 # new | reused | modified, against the baseline
test_impacts:
  - test: { repository: claims-api, tier: component, id: Claims.ExpiredClaimIsAccepted }
    change: removed
    reason: Its expectation contradicts VR-001.
    replaced_by: [Claims.ExpiredClaimIsRejected]
```

## Satisfaction

A method is satisfied when its claimed tests exist, their `change` is allowed,
a review accepted this exact claims revision where `semantic_review: required`,
and every claimed test passed in the engine's results at the method's
repository and tier. A skipped test does not pass. A criterion is satisfied when
all its methods are; a requirement when all its supporting criteria are.
